completeness_assessment.issue: CAMPAIGNS table has no documented relationships in the semantic model, despite being present in the glossary with foreign key references implied by business context
completeness_assessment.recommendation: Add relationship documentation for CAMPAIGNS table showing how it relates to CUSTOMERS (via target_segment matching customer_segment) or ORDERS (via campaign period overlap with order_date)

completeness_assessment.issue: No metrics defined for campaign effectiveness analysis (e.g., revenue during campaign period, campaign ROI, conversion rate by campaign)
completeness_assessment.recommendation: Define campaign-specific metrics such as campaign_revenue_usd, campaign_conversion_rate, and campaign_roi to enable marketing analytics

completeness_assessment.issue: CUSTOMER_ACCOUNT_MANAGERS SCD Type-2 temporal join is documented in relationships but no metrics demonstrate its usage

efficiency_assessment.issue: total_revenue_usd and item_level_revenue_usd metrics use similar aggregation patterns but are defined separately with duplicated logic for summing revenue amounts
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Consider creating a reusable base CTE or view that can be referenced by both order-level and item-level revenue metrics to reduce code duplication

efficiency_assessment.issue: top_products_by_revenue and top_customers_by_revenue metrics use identical RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(...) DESC) pattern with only the grouping columns differing
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Extract the ranking logic into a reusable pattern or template that can be parameterized by entity type (product, customer, category, etc.)

efficiency_assessment.issue: Multiple metrics calculate similar profit/margin calculations (gross_profit_usd, gross_margin_pct, item_level_profit_usd) with repeated subtraction logic
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Consider defining a base profit calculation function or CTE that can be reused across order-level and item-level profit metrics

efficiency_assessment.issue: Monthly revenue metric (monthly_revenue_usd) could be generalized to support multiple time grains (daily, weekly, quarterly, yearly) rather than having separate metric definitions for each grain
efficiency_assessment.recommendation: Create a parameterized time-series revenue metric that accepts a grain parameter (day, week, month, quarter, year) to enable flexible temporal analysis without metric proliferation
